Marginalia, Briefly

The margin is where a book talks back. Every serious reader has argued with a page in pencil, and every library has a shelf of books whose most valuable words are not the printer's.

Write in the margin the way you would speak to the author across a table: briefly, specifically, and with the page open between you.

A book is a machine to think with.

See also the commonplace book.
